metaDescription: Six corded electric wood chippers from 1.5 to 2.5 inch capacity compared on motor power, reduction ratio, blades, bag size and extension cord needs.
expertTake: The Earthwise GS70015 is the best all round pick for ordinary pruning, because it is honest about capacity and gives real extension cord guidance. The Patriot CSV-2515 is the choice for anyone with limbs thicker than 2 inches who still wants no engine. The Westinghouse is the pick if you need a light machine. If your trees drop limbs thicker than about 2.5 inches, skip electric chippers entirely and buy a gas machine.
introParagraphs: An electric wood chipper is a plug-in machine that feeds branches into a spinning blade and spits out chips. The motors are modest, the branch capacity is limited and the box often promises more than the hopper can deliver. The most common mistake is buying for the biggest limb you might ever cut, then using the machine on soft green material it handles poorly.

This guide explains how motor power, blade design, reduction ratio and extension cords actually decide what a corded chipper can do. Start with the picks above for the short list, then read the reviews below to match a machine to your own trees, your nearest outlet, your storage space and the kind of debris your yard actually produces.

products.name: Earthwise GS70015 15 Amp Corded Electric Chipper Shredder

specList.label: Cord advice
specList.value: 12 AWG up to 75 ft, 10 AWG for longer

products.description:
The Earthwise GS70015 earns the top spot because it is honest about what a 15 amp chipper is. It chips green and dry branches up to roughly 1.5 to 1.8 inches and the maker says plainly that it performs best on dry, seasoned material, since wet, freshly cut stems carry more moisture and slow the blades. That candor is useful, because the biggest source of disappointment with electric chippers is feeding them the wrong debris.

The motor is a 15 amp unit, and the listing gives real extension cord guidance: 12 gauge up to 75 ft, or 10 gauge for longer runs. That matters because a thin cord drops voltage under load, and a motor starved of voltage runs hot, loses torque and jams more. Heat-treated SK5 steel blades, a 15:1 reduction ratio and an interlock switch between the cover and body that cuts power when opened are sensible for the class. Compared with the Patriot, which handles about 2.5 inches, the Earthwise gives up a full inch of branch size but is far lighter and simpler.

Ownership is easy. The blades arrive coated in anti-rust oil, so wipe it off before first use, and keep the edges oiled when storing for winter. Flip or replace the SK5 blades when chips turn from coin-shaped to shredded. The 10.5 gallon bag is the smallest in this lineup, so on a big cleanup you will empty it often, but wheels and a compact body make storage in a shed easy.
products.bestFor: Homeowners with ordinary pruning debris of up to about 1.5 inches who want a plug-in machine with clear guidance.
pros: Maker gives clear extension cord gauge and length advice
Heat-treated SK5 blades are easy to inspect and replace
Interlock switch cuts power when the hopper cover opens
Compact and light enough for one person to wheel around
cons: Smallest collection bag here at 10.5 gallons, so frequent emptying
Branch capacity tops out near 1.8 inches, no thicker limbs
Green or wet material reduces chipping efficiency noticeably

products.name: Patriot CSV-2515 1.5 HP Corded Electric Chipper Shredder
products.description:
The Patriot CSV-2515 is the heavy hitter of the plug-in class. Its listing quotes branches up to 2.5 inches, a full inch more than the 15 amp machines at 1.5 to 1.8 inches, and it makes coin-sized chips rather than finely shredded fibres. It is rated at 1.5 horsepower, which is an unusually direct way to state motor output when most rivals quote only amps.

A large top hopper takes leaves and bulky yard waste, while the side discharge into a standard collection bag keeps chips flowing. The motor is described as quiet and maintenance free, and it starts with a flip of a switch, so there is no carburetor, no fuel and no pull cord to maintain. Compared with the Earthwise, it is the better choice if you routinely prune thumb-thick or slightly thicker limbs, but it is a more serious machine and the premium price tier in this lineup reflects that.

The trade is portability and cost. A machine built to run a 1.5 HP motor continuously is bulkier than the plastic-bodied 15 amp units, and you still need a heavy gauge extension cord to protect the motor. Plan to keep it near an outlet, wear eye and ear protection and feed branches butt end first so the blade pulls them in. If most of your debris is under 1.5 inches, the cheaper machines here will do the same work.
products.bestFor: Owners with orchard or hedge pruning who regularly cut limbs thicker than 2 inches but want no engine.
pros: Handles branches up to 2.5 in, the largest electric capacity here
Rated by horsepower instead of only amps, so output is clear
Quiet, maintenance free motor with no fuel or oil to manage
Large top hopper takes leaves and bulky yard waste
cons: Priced like a premium machine compared with the 15 amp units
Heavier and bulkier than the plastic bodied chippers
Still tied to an outlet and a heavy gauge extension cord

products.name: LawnMaster FD1504 15 Amp Electric Wood Chipper, 1.8 In

specList.label: Storage
specList.value: Removable axle folds size by about half

products.description:
The LawnMaster FD1504 is the pick for anyone who has to put the machine in a small garage or shed. A removable axle assembly reduces its footprint by roughly half, which is a rare, practical design choice among chippers that usually take up a lot of floor. It takes branches to 1.8 inches with a 15 amp motor and a two-sided blade spinning at about 3,700 RPM.

The reduction ratio is 16:1, so sixteen bags of bulky yard debris become about one bag of mulch, a step up from the 14:1 of its FD1503 sibling. It comes with a push paddle, a blade changing tool and a 12 gallon collection bin, and the dent-resistant polypropylene body is light. Compared with the Westinghouse, it has a similar capacity but a slightly different RPM figure and a more storage-friendly build, while the Keenstone claims a higher 21:1 ratio.

In use, a two-sided blade means you can flip the cutting edge before replacing it, which stretches blade life. Remove the axle and wheels before storing, keep the blade lightly oiled and use the push paddle for the last few inches of a branch. Like every machine in this class, it is meant for small limbs and prunings, not for ripping through a storm-fallen oak.
products.bestFor: Small garages and sheds where the folded storage size matters as much as chipping power.
pros: Removable axle shrinks the stored footprint by about half
16:1 reduction ratio cuts yard waste volume sharply
Two-sided blade can be flipped before it is replaced
Push paddle and blade changing tool come in the box
cons: Branch capacity of 1.8 in is the same as cheaper rivals
Polypropylene housing is light but not as rugged as steel
The 12 gallon bin fills quickly on a large cleanup

products.name: Keenstone 15 Amp Electric Wood Chipper, 1.8 In, 21:1

specList.label: Blades
specList.value: SK5 carbon steel, dual edge, spare set

products.description:
The Keenstone pushes the usual 15 amp formula with a 21:1 reduction ratio, the highest on the page, and a 4,000 RPM blade system. That ratio means twenty-one bags of bulky brush shrink to one, which is helpful for composting or mulching where volume matters. It handles branches up to 1.8 inches, the same as the other 15 amp machines.

Where it differs is in the extras. The SK5 carbon steel blades are dual edged with a spare set included, a 50 L bag gives more room than the Earthwise bag, and a 3 year warranty is the longest of the budget machines. Overcurrent and thermal overload protection plus a safety interlock round out the safeguards. The listing also says a rotating blade system helps draw branches downward, so you push less compared with a simple paddle design like the LawnMaster.

The limits are those of the class: avoid leaves, bamboo, vines, roots, hay, straw and frozen branches, because soft or stringy material wraps the blades and jams the hopper. An openable cutting chamber and cleanout opening make clearing a jam easier. Keep the blades sharp and flip the edge when chips look torn instead of cut.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want the most volume reduction and the longest warranty from a plug-in chipper.
pros: 21:1 reduction ratio is the highest in this lineup
Three year warranty is longer than most budget machines
Spare dual edge SK5 blade set is included in the box
Large 50 L bag holds far more than the Earthwise bag
cons: Branch capacity is still limited to 1.8 inches of wood
Soft or stringy debris such as vines will jam the hopper
Newer brand name with little track record to judge

products.name: Westinghouse 1.7 In 15 Amp Corded Electric Wood Chipper
products.description:
The Westinghouse corded chipper is the lightest machine here at 19.2 pounds, which makes it the easy one to carry over a step or load into a car trunk. It runs a 15 amp motor at up to 4,000 RPM and takes branches up to 1.7 inches, slightly less than the 1.8 inch rivals. A dual hole feed hopper lets you send larger branches down one chute and smaller twigs down the other.

SK5 steel blades, a safety interlock, overload protection and a no-wait restart feature round out a typical but sound spec. A 2 year limited warranty and lifetime technical support are better than the 1 year found on many no-name machines. Compared with the Earthwise, it is lighter and has a larger 12 gallon bag, but it gives up a small amount of capacity, and compared with the Patriot it is a much smaller machine.

Because it is so light, it can tip or creep when you feed a stiff branch, so brace the machine and feed steadily. Use a 12 gauge cord, keep a spare blade on hand and clean the hopper after each session. It suits renters, small lots and anyone who prunes shrubs more than trees.
products.bestFor: Small lots and people who need a light machine they can carry and store easily.
pros: Only 19.2 lb, the lightest chipper in this comparison
Dual hole hopper separates thick branches from small twigs
Two year warranty plus lifetime technical support line
No-wait restart after an overload shutdown trips it
cons: Capacity of 1.7 in is a touch below the 1.8 in machines
Light body can creep when you feed in a stiff branch
Bag is noticeably smaller than the 50 L bag on the Keenstone

products.name: Sun Joe CJ603E 15 Amp Wood Chipper Shredder, 1.7 In

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Hopper and locking knob halt operation when opened

products.description:
The Sun Joe CJ603E is a straightforward 15 amp shredder with a 1.7 inch capacity and a well-known consumer brand behind it. The listing says it reduces branches to about one twenty-first of the original volume, and a locking knob on the hopper stops operation the moment the hopper is opened. That integrated safety design is the part that matters most when you reach in to clear a jam.

Its design is compact and designed for easy assembly, with 7 inch wheels for moving it around the yard and a collection bag included. Against the LawnMaster FD1504, it gives similar capacity but lacks the axle storage trick, and compared with the Keenstone it lists less about warranty terms and bag size. Sun Joe markets it as quiet in operation, which is relative: it is still a loud shredder compared with a hand pruner.

For ownership, keep the blades sharp and the hopper clear of wet leaves, which clog the cutting chamber. Use a 12 gauge extension cord, and treat the 1.7 inch rating as a maximum for dry hardwood, not freshly cut green wood. It is a good choice for seasonal cleanup in a typical suburban yard.
products.bestFor: Suburban gardeners who want a familiar brand and a solid safety lock on the hopper.
pros: Locking hopper knob halts operation when the hopper opens
Recognized consumer brand with wide parts availability
Compact body with 7 in wheels for moving around the yard
Reduces yard waste volume to a fraction of the original
cons: Branch capacity of 1.7 in limits it to small prunings
Listing offers less detail on bag size and warranty
Still a loud machine despite the quiet operation claim

buyingCriteria.explanation: Branch capacity is the diameter a machine can chip, and corded electric models run from about 1.5 to 2.5 inches. Most 15 amp units here cap at 1.7 to 1.8 inches, while the Patriot CSV-2515 handles up to 2.5 inches. Measure the thickest limb you prune, not the average one, and add a margin because hardwood is harder than softwood. Buyers often assume a 1.8 inch label means any 1.8 inch limb, but dense dry oak at that size will stall a 15 amp motor.

Most corded chippers use a 15 amp motor, which on a 120 volt household circuit draws about 1,800 watts. That is also the limit of a standard 15 amp breaker, so running another heavy tool on the same circuit can trip it. The Patriot lists 1.5 horsepower instead of amps, which is a clearer description of output. Choose the machine whose rating matches the size of limbs you cut, and do not expect any 15 amp unit to behave like a 7 HP gas engine.

A thin extension cord drops voltage under load, and a motor starved of voltage runs hotter, makes less torque and jams more. The Earthwise maker recommends 12 gauge cord up to 75 ft and 10 gauge for longer runs. A 16 gauge garden cord that works fine for a hedge trimmer can damage a chipper motor. Buy a short, heavy cord with the machine and plug it into a dedicated outlet where possible.

Reduction ratio is how much the volume shrinks, such as 21:1 on the Keenstone, 16:1 on the LawnMaster FD1504 and 15:1 on the Earthwise. A higher ratio means fewer bags to empty but it depends on debris. Look for dual edged SK5 blades that can be flipped, and for spare blades in the box. Sharp blades cut chips, while dull blades tear and bind branches, and that is the main cause of motor strain.

Electric chippers are built for dry or seasoned woody prunings, not leaves, vines, bamboo, roots, hay or frozen branches. Soft or stringy material wraps the blade and jams the hopper. The Earthwise and Keenstone listings both advise this, and green wood with high moisture slows the blades. If your yard produces lots of green hedge clippings and leaves, a shredder with a larger top hopper, such as the Patriot, suits better than a branch-focused unit.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Look at weight, storage and safety
buyingCriteria.explanation: A 19.2 lb machine like the Westinghouse is easy to carry, while the LawnMaster FD1504 folds to about half its size by removing the axle. Safety features that matter are an interlock that cuts power when the hopper opens, overload protection and a push paddle. Never reach into the hopper with your hand, and always wear eye and ear protection. Check bag size too, since the 10.5 gallon Earthwise bag fills much faster than the 50 L Keenstone bag.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum branch diameter a manufacturer says the machine can chip, usually measured on dry softwood. It is a ceiling set by the blade size, hopper opening and motor torque. Dense or green wood reduces the practical limit.
specDecoder.watchFor: A label of 1.8 inches on most 15 amp units is a best case. The Earthwise lists a range of 1.5 to 1.8 inches, which is the more honest way to say it.

specDecoder.meaning: Amps are the electric current the motor draws, and horsepower is the output. A 15 amp motor at 120 volts draws about 1,800 watts and is limited by the household breaker. The Patriot lists 1.5 HP, which is a direct output figure.
specDecoder.watchFor: Amps do not tell you torque. Two 15 amp chippers can behave differently depending on gearing, blade RPM and build quality.

specDecoder.meaning: The ratio compares the volume of the original debris to the volume of the chips. A 21:1 ratio means a pile reduces to roughly one twenty-first of its size. It depends on the debris type and how finely the blade chops.
specDecoder.watchFor: The ratio is measured on ideal material. The Keenstone's 21:1 and the LawnMaster's 16:1 will be lower with leafy or wet debris.

specDecoder.meaning: Blade speed in rotations per minute decides how cleanly the blade slices the branch. The Keenstone and Westinghouse quote about 4,000 RPM and the LawnMaster about 3,700 RPM. Higher speed gives a cleaner cut but needs sharp blades.
specDecoder.watchFor: RPM is not torque. A faster blade does not help if the motor stalls under load.

specDecoder.meaning: American Wire Gauge describes wire thickness, where a lower number means a thicker wire. A 12 AWG cord carries 15 amps with little voltage drop up to about 75 ft, as the Earthwise maker advises. Thinner cords overheat and starve the motor.
specDecoder.watchFor: Cord packaging often shows a maximum amp rating that applies only to short lengths. Match the gauge to both amps and length.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and motor output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated branch capacity and motor ratings, from the 1.7 inch Westinghouse and Sun Joe to the 2.5 inch Patriot. Where the listing gave horsepower or a capacity range, we gave it more weight than a bare amp figure. We treated every capacity number as a ceiling for dry wood.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blades and jam resistance
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed blade steel, edge design and feed systems. SK5 dual edge blades, spare sets and a feed that draws branches in, as on the Keenstone, ranked higher. Safety interlocks and openable cutting chambers counted because jams are the normal failure of this class.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power supply realism
howWeEvaluated.description: We read the listings for cord guidance, overload protection and breaker limits, since a corded chipper is only as good as its supply. The Earthwise gives clear gauge advice, which raised its rank. Machines that gave no cord advice were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared weight, wheels, bag size and folded size. The Westinghouse at 19.2 lb and the LawnMaster FD1504 with its removable axle lead on handling. The Earthwise's 10.5 gallon bag is the smallest, and the Keenstone's 50 L the largest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Warranty and lineup value
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each machine in the lineup by capacity and extras. The Patriot leads on capacity, the Keenstone on warranty and reduction ratio, and the Earthwise on documentation. We looked at warranty terms where listed, such as the 3 year Keenstone and 2 year Westinghouse.

howToChoose.intro: The real trade is convenience against capacity.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: Corded machines such as the Earthwise, Westinghouse and Keenstone start with a switch, have no fuel to stale and run quietly compared with gas. They are limited to roughly 1.5 to 2.5 inches and tied to a cord. They suit small yards and suburban lots.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: A gas chipper with a 7 HP engine takes 3 inch limbs and works anywhere, but needs fuel, oil and carburetor care. It is louder, heavier and costs more. Choose gas if you have trees that drop limbs thicker than 2.5 inches.

howToChoose.note: Pick electric if your limbs are under 2 inches and you have an outlet. Pick gas if you regularly cut thicker wood or work far from power.

howToChoose.intro: Plan the power before you buy.

rows: States 12 AWG to 75 ft and 10 AWG beyond
1.5 HP motor suits a heavy gauge cord

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Yard cleanup produces twigs, small branches and some leaves, so look for a large collection bag, a high reduction ratio and a hopper that takes small material. Avoid wet green debris, which clogs any 15 amp machine.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Keenstone 21:1 with a 50 L bag is the best for volume reduction, and the Patriot's large top hopper is best for mixed leaves and twigs. The LawnMaster FD1504 is the pick when storage space is tight.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you prune limbs thicker than 2 inches or run the machine often. The Patriot CSV-2515 offers the largest capacity and a horsepower rating, and the Keenstone adds a 3 year warranty for frequent use.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you only clear twigs once or twice a season. The Westinghouse, the LawnMaster FD1504 and the Sun Joe CJ603E handle light prunings without the weight and cost of a heavier unit.

maintenance.interval: After every few hours of use
maintenance.why: Dull blades tear and bind branches, which strains the motor. Flip dual edged blades or replace the pair.
Packed wet chips cling to the blade and rust it. Open the hopper and brush out the chamber.
Bare steel rusts in damp sheds. A light coat of oil protects the edge.
A nicked cord or loose plug can overheat. Replace any damaged cord before use.
Vibration loosens blade bolts and axle hardware. Tighten them with the unit unplugged.
Damp chips mold in the bag and clog the mesh. Shake out and dry before storing.

faq.q: Can an electric chipper handle 2 inch branches?
faq.a: Most 15 amp chippers are rated for 1.5 to 1.8 inches, so a 2 inch limb is beyond their rating. The Patriot CSV-2515 lists 2.5 inches. For thicker green wood, a gas machine is the safer choice.

faq.q: How much do I really save with a higher reduction ratio?
faq.a: A 21:1 ratio means a pile shrinks to a smaller volume than a 15:1 machine, so you empty fewer bags. It works best on dry woody debris. Wet or leafy material lowers the real ratio, so treat it as a best case.

faq.q: How long do chipper blades last?
faq.a: It depends on use, but blades dull faster on dirty or sandy wood. Dual edged SK5 blades can be flipped to extend life, and the Keenstone includes a spare set. Replace blades when the chips look torn instead of cut.

faq.q: Why does my electric chipper keep jamming?
faq.a: Common causes are dull blades, wet or stringy material, a thin extension cord and feeding too fast. Use dry wood, a 12 gauge cord and a steady feed. Clean out the chamber after each use.

faq.q: Is it safe to use a chipper in the rain?
faq.a: No. Corded electric tools should not be used in wet conditions or on wet ground. Some units have water resistance ratings, but you should still keep the cord and plug dry and use a GFCI outlet.

faq.q: Can I use the chips as mulch?
faq.a: Yes, fresh chips make a good path covering or mulch around established plants. Keep a few inches away from tree trunks and let green chips age before using them on vegetable beds. Dry, aged chips are better for compost.
